title: Pragmatic SDK retry presets, idempotency contract, and failure taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: define pragmatic, language-appropriate retry/backoff defaults, a minimal idempotency contract across HTTP and streaming endpoints, and a clear retryable-error taxonomy for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket captures the cross-SDK proposal, examples, rollout plan, and acceptance criteria.

Rationale: teams repeatedly implement slightly incompatible retry semantics and idempotency handling. Differences cause surprising duplicate downstream effects, inconsistent user experience, and operational complexity for Redwood. A single pragmatic set of defaults + a lightweight idempotency contract will reduce incidents and simplify user guidance while allowing opt-out and tuning for advanced use cases.
acceptance_criteria: Consensus design doc approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go)
Default retry/backoff presets implemented in all three SDKs behind a feature flag and documented
Idempotency header semantics implemented for non-streaming write-like endpoints with a 24h dedup window and clear error responses
Retryable error taxonomy published and used by SDKs to classify server responses
Streaming resume semantics documented and an ergonomic resume-token example provided for each SDK
Integration tests covering at-least-once vs at-most-once scenarios and key edge cases added to SDK CI
implementation_plan:
1) Design: finalize taxonomy and idempotency contract in this ticket. 2) Engine: add standardized error codes/markers consumed by SDKs. 3) SDK changes: add RetryPolicy helper, default presets, idempotency header handling, and streaming resume helpers in parallel branches for Python/TS/Go. 4) QA: run fuzz and e2e scenarios (transient, rate-limit, cancel during body upload). 5) Rollout: behind feature flag per SDK; dogfood within Redwood services; enable by default in next minor release after 2 weeks of dogfooding.

Language-specific notes included in the examples field. All changes must be behind opt-out flags until the rollout window completes.
examples: Idempotency header: Use header 'Idempotency-Key: <uuid>' for all non-idempotent POST/PUT endpoints. Server returns 409 + 'Idempotency-Status: applied|duplicate' when a duplicate is detected. Client behavior: do not retry non-idempotent calls without a key. If key present, safe to retry on retryable errors until server returns success or explicit duplicate error.

Retry presets (default):
- fast-interactive: max_retries=3, base_delay=50ms, max_delay=500ms, jitter=full, backoff=exponential (recommended for UI calls)
- throughput: max_retries=2, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=2s, jitter=equal, backoff=exponential (recommended for batch/embedding workloads)
- conservative: max_retries=5, base_delay=100ms, max_delay=5s, jitter=full, backoff=exponential+cap (for flaky networks)
Clients can override per-call or set SDK-level defaults.

Retryable error taxonomy (summary):
- TRANSIENT: 5xx (500, 502, 503, 504) and connection resets -> retry with backoff
- RATE_LIMIT: 429 with Retry-After or quota marker -> respect Retry-After; consider route-level fallback rather than aggressive retry
- THROTTLE_SOFT: 429 without Retry-After -> small backoff + lower concurrency; retry preset: throughput
- CLIENT_ERROR_NONRETRY: 4xx (400, 401, 403) except 429 -> do NOT retry by default; surface to caller
- IDENTITY_EXPIRED: 401 with specific token-expiration code -> refresh token and retry once
- STREAM_INTERRUPT: streaming transport-level interruptions should use resume tokens when available; otherwise surface as TRANSIENT for short-lived streams
Each SDK will map server response bodies and headers into this taxonomy rather than relying solely on numeric codes.

Idempotency window: Server deduplicates for 24 hours by default. SDKs should optionally allow overriding idempotency_expiry_seconds in client config for advanced users. Shorter expiration reduces dedupe benefits; longer increases storage cost.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: RetryPolicy simulator that injects transient failures and asserts backoff behavior in all SDKs.
- Integration: Run SDKs against staging runtime with injected 429/5xx errors and idempotency simulation.
- Streaming tests: simulate mid-stream drop and verify resume token works across SDKs.
- Load tests: ensure default presets do not cause retries to amplify load on overloaded endpoints.
- Observability: add metrics for retry counts, idempotency duplicate rate, and resumed stream success rate.

review_feedback: Lin Wei (Go SDK): prefer default base_delay=75ms for fast-interactive to match language GC characteristics
Sophie Turner (PM): call out UX for developers when idempotency key reused across logically different operations
Security (Maya Rao): confirm idempotency key is treated as non-sensitive and not logged; redact in debug logs
risk_assessment: Medium risk. Main risks: (1) premature enablement could increase load via retry storms; mitigations: feature flags and conservative defaults. (2) idempotency semantics could be misused across multi-step operations; mitigations: clear docs and examples. (3) streaming resume semantics require runtime support and version negotiation; mitigations: graceful fallback to full-retry on older runtimes.
notes: Prefer readable defaults over perfect theoretical ones; most customers won't tune these.
Document migration path: opt-in flag -> dogfood -> enable-by-default after telemetry review
